video_title: Knicks vs. Spurs NBA Finals Matchup 🍿 Wemby shines, OKC's future & Robinson's injury | SportsCenter

quotes.speaker: Victor Wembanyama
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama on the emotional weight of reaching the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: That's the definition of a winning play. It's whoever wanted it more.
quotes.quote: I was so stoked. I was so proud of him, so happy. That's the definition of a winning play. It's whoever wanted it more. All these hours we put in, it's for this type of emotions. I want to win so bad. It's like my life depends on it.

quotes.speaker: Quentin Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Quentin Richardson on Victor Wembanyama's need for aggressive play
quotes.excerpt: I think he needs to keep his foot on the gas, keep attacking, stay close to the basket.
quotes.quote: For me it's going to definitely be him being aggressive and continuing to attack and be close to that basket and getting into the paint because I'm not saying he can't shoot the three, but I don't want to see him settle. Sometimes he can get comfortable with it or if things get tough or if he gets tired, you can settle for that three because he can easily make it. But I think he needs to keep his foot on the gas, keep attacking, stay close to the basket, stay attacking the basket and getting close to that paint as possible as much as possible and I think for him that's going to be big returns if he can do that.

quotes.speaker: Dylan Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Dylan Harper's impact as a rookie for the San Antonio Spurs
quotes.excerpt: He's a major player on this team despite being drafted 11 months ago.
quotes.quote: Dylan Harper, 20-year-old rookie from the Jersey area, went to Rutgers. We know that MSG and New York City are the basketball mecca to everybody, but particularly to people from that area and Dylan Harper talked about last night dreaming as growing up of playing in the NBA Finals in Madison Square Garden. The two crazy parts of it is he'll be on the opponent. He's on the San Antonio Spurs, but also this is not some quiet rookie who's on the back end of a rotation who's just kind of getting his taste in the league. Like he's a major player on this team despite being drafted 11 months ago.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill

text_blocks.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
text_blocks.text: Well, Mitchell Robinson only plays 15 minutes a night and he can't shoot and he doesn't handle the ball much, but there's so much importance on what a guy like him does because he's going to have to defend Victor Wembanyama. He's going to put that big body on him. Hopefully for the Knicks, Karl-Anthony Towns can stay out of foul trouble. That's where his importance is because they've never played anything like Victor Wembanyama.

text_blocks.speaker: Quentin Richardson
text_blocks.text: I still see him being a big playing a big role in this series. I don't think that impacts the fact that he has to go out there and be physical against Wemby, be a presence in that paint, still go get offensive rebound like he does at such an elite level and again, he has six fouls that he has to use on Wemby. At the end of the day, he's there to provide relief for the big guys for Karl-Anthony Towns on that interior and to come in and present a paint presence for the Knicks and I think he still has a high likelihood to do that even with the injury to his hand.

quotes.summary_phrase: Quentin Richardson predicts Karl-Anthony Towns as Finals MVP
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to say Karl-Anthony Towns will be the MVP.
quotes.quote: I'm going to say Karl-Anthony Towns will be the MVP. That's bold enough for you, Vinnie?
